explanation: The theorem is about the library's own definitions: AlgebraicCurve.Place, CanonicalLocalResidueDataK.res, differentialCoeff, poleSubmodule, laurentTailCoeff and uniformizer. It says the residue of dg is zero for g with a pole of order at most N. The proof is an induction that peels off the leading Laurent coefficient using library-specific lemmas. I did not run any searches. Mathlib has no residue-of-differential theory for places of function fields or Laurent-tail machinery, so I do not expect a matching declaration. I found none.
